items.prose: Macerating sixty kilograms of chopped white linen rags between the phosphor-bronze bedplate knives and the sixty-RPM revolving roll fibrillated the fibers without shortening. The resulting creamy stock had high internal fiber-to-fiber bonding strength.

Adjusting the screw-wheel bedplate gap to exactly 0.25mm regulated stock freeness to 42° Schopper-Riegler. The fine degree of hydration allowed fast water drainage across wire moulds while retaining tight sheet formation.

A revolving hexagonal drum clad in 60-mesh brass wire gauze skimmed dirty wash water from the center trough while retaining pulp. Fresh spring water flushed through the oval tub until the effluent ran crystal-clear.

Processing tough hemp canvas with wooden-backed dull roll bars combed out ten-millimeter long bast fibers without severing them. The long-fibered pulp was reserved for high-tensile technical drawing paper and filter membranes.

Circulating pulp slurry over the curved backfall crest broke up un-macerated seam knots and cotton twist clumps. The homogeneous fiber suspension showed zero floating clots when diluted in inspection glass cylinders.

Shredded pre-war diazo and cyanotype blueprints were soaked in 2% warm soda ash liquor to decompose Prussian blue ferric ferrocyanide dyes. Three subsequent freshwater wash cycles converted the dark scrap into pristine cream-colored pulp.

Inspecting the thirty-two cast bronze flybars revealed rounded edges and cavitation pits along leading corners. Dressing the bars with silicon carbide stones restored sharp, burr-free bevels, reducing beating power consumption by 22%.

Dosing the finished linen pulp with 6% precipitated calcium carbonate provided a built-in alkaline buffer. The alkaline reserve guaranteed that finished bunker ledger sheets will resist acid deterioration and yellowing for over five centuries.
